entries.title: I Corinthians 12:1
segments: In the next place, Brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant about spiritual gifts.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:2
segments: You know that there was a time when you were Gentiles, going astray after idols that could not speak, just as you happened to be led.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:3
segments: Therefore I tell you plainly that no one who speaks under the influence of the Spirit of God says 'JESUS IS ACCURSED,' and that no one can say 'JESUS IS LORD,' except under the influence of the Holy Spirit.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:4
segments: Gifts differ, but the Spirit is the same;

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:5
segments: Ways of serving differ, yet the Master is the same;

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:6
segments: Results differ, yet the God who brings about every result is in every case the same.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:7
segments: To each man there is given spiritual illumination for the general good.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:8
segments: To one is given the power to speak with wisdom through the Spirit; to another the power to speak with knowledge, due to the same Spirit;

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:9
segments: To another faith by the same Spirit; to another power to cure diseases by the one Spirit; to another supernatural powers;

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:10
segments: To another the gift of preaching; to another the gift of distinguishing between true and false inspiration; to another varieties of the gift of 'tongues'; to another the power to interpret 'tongues.'

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:11
segments: All these result from one and the same Spirit, who distributes his gifts to each individually as he wills.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:12
segments: For just as the human body is one whole, and yet has many parts, and all its parts, many though they are, form but one body, so it is with the Christ;

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:13
segments: For it was by one Spirit that we were all baptized to form one Body, whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free men, and were all imbued with one Spirit.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:14
segments: The human body, I repeat, consists not of one part, but of many.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:15
segments: If the foot says 'Since I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,' it does not on that account cease to belong to the body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:16
segments: Or if the ear says 'Since I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,' it does not on that account cease to belong to the body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:17
segments: If all the body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If it were all hearing, where would the sense of smell be?

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:18
segments: But in fact God has placed each individual part just where he thought fit in the body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:19
segments: If, however, they all made up only one part, where would the body be?

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:20
segments: But in fact, although it has many parts, there is only one body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:21
segments: The eye cannot say to the hand 'I do not need you,' nor, again, the head to the feet 'I do not need you.'

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:22
segments: No! Those parts of the body that seem naturally the weaker are indispensable;

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:23
segments: And those parts which we deem less honorable we surround with special honor; and our ungraceful parts receive a special grace which our graceful parts do not require.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:24
segments: Yes, God has so constructed the body--by giving a special honor to the part that lacks it-

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:25
segments: As to secure that there should be no disunion in the body, but that the parts should show the same care for one another.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:26
segments: If one part suffers, all the others suffer with it, and if one part has honor done it, all the others share its joy.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:27
segments: Together you are the Body of Christ, and individually its parts.

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:28
segments: In the Church God has appointed, first, Apostles, secondly Preachers, thirdly Teachers; then he has given supernatural powers, then power to cure diseases, aptness for helping others, capacity to govern, varieties of the gift of 'tongues.'

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:29
segments: Can every one be an Apostle? can every one be a Preacher? can every one be a Teacher? can every one have supernatural powers?

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:30
segments: Can every one have power to cure diseases? can every one speak in 'tongues'? can every one interpret them?

entries.title: I Corinthians 12:31
segments: Strive for the greater gifts. Yet I can still show you a way beyond all comparison the best.
